items.title: Pay 'import duties' to release held parcel
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date for payment: 09.11.2026. No period to count and no deemed-delivery rule applies, since this sender is a company/private party (not a German authority) and the date is printed explicitly. Taken as written: due date = 2026-11-09.

warnings: The IBAN given for payment (DE96 7001 0080 0661 2345 67) fails the standard checksum check, meaning it is very likely mistyped or fabricated — do not transfer money to it.

The payee is a private company ('Intl. Parcel Clearance Ltd.'), not Zoll or Deutsche Post/DHL; real German import-duty demands for parcels are issued by customs or the delivering carrier, not by a separate 'Paketzentrum Zollabwicklung' firm.

The letter asks for queries 'ausschließlich per WhatsApp' to a mobile number, with no landline, no official case handler and no postal reply option — this is a common pattern in parcel/customs scam letters.

The very short payment window (4 days from the letter's date) combined with a threat to return or destroy the parcel is a pressure tactic typical of fee scams; verify the shipment status directly with the actual carrier (DHL, DPD, etc.) or the Zollamt before paying anything.

Overall this letter shows several hallmarks of a fake customs/parcel-release scam; recommend not paying and instead checking with the real shipping company or reporting it, rather than treating the printed deadline as a genuine legal obligation.
